notes: BurnTaxHook takes the chain PoolManager and the deployed BurnTaxToken in that order. Every enabled callback and unlockCallback accept only the immutable PoolManager; beforeInitialize returns its selector, accepts LP fees 500, 3000 and 10000 and refuses the dynamic flag and every other fee. Deploy the token first, mine a CREATE2 hook address with permission bits 0x20cc under mask 0x3fff, then deploy the hook and initialize its pool atomically on a Cancun-compatible EVM. The launch pool has native ETH as currency0 and BTAX as currency1, with the pool's unchanged 0.3% LP fee and tick spacing 60. Initial-price assumption, since the brief specifies none: sqrtPriceX96 = 2^96, matching the test reference price, gives 1 BTAX per ETH before swap costs because both currencies have 18 decimals; it is not a valuation guarantee. On each successful swap containing the configured token, positive hook return deltas charge floor(gross BTAX / 100), where gross means pool output on buys and total trader payment on sells. Exact-input sells reserve the tax from the specified input; exact-input buys deduct it from actual BTAX output. Exact-output buys gross up the requested net BTAX output and exact-output sells gross up actual pool BTAX input, using tax = floor((net - 1) / 99) for positive net and zero otherwise. Burned(bytes32 indexed poolId, bool indexed isBuy, uint256 amount) reports true for buys, false for sells, and BTAX minor units, including zero-tax dust. Burn funding: when the PoolManager's BTAX balance covers the tax (every buy and the usual sell) PoolManager.take sends it to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD in the same swap. When it does not (an ordinary router settles the seller's BTAX only after afterSwap, so a fresh manager or a launch pool whose in-range BTAX was bought out can be short), the hook mints the tax to itself as an ERC-6909 claim instead and also emits BurnDeferred(bytes32 indexed poolId, uint256 amount); the trader's delta is identical and the swap does not revert. pendingBurn() shows the deferred amount; burnPending() is permissionless and transfers the whole claim to DEAD, emitting DeferredBurnSettled(uint256 amount), and the next covered swap redeems it on its own. The claim can go nowhere but DEAD: the hook has no transfer, approval or operator function for it. No native ETH is ever moved to DEAD, so a recipient that rejects ETH cannot arise. Token-only seeded pools support buys with zero native ETH in the manager. Taxed exact-input sells and exact-output buys revert on partial fills (PartialFillWithSpecifiedTax); the other two modes tax actual execution. Pools without BTAX get zero hook deltas and no events. Transfers, liquidity operations and pools selecting another hook are outside the tax. Routers must enforce slippage on final trader deltas. The token has no constructor arguments and no post-deployment mint path; sending to DEAD leaves totalSupply unchanged. Neither contract has owner, admin, upgrade, withdrawal or tax-setting functions. README.md describes the rule, rounding, deferred burns and limits. Supply and allocation policy are outside this manifest.
